title: B2 First for Schools Sample Paper 1

partner.name: Oliver
partner.persona: A 16-year-old sixth-form student from Cambridge preparing for B2 First for Schools. Speaks natural British English, sometimes changes his mind mid-discussion, and asks follow-up questions.

1.opening: First we'd like to know something about you.

questions.text: Who are you most like in your family? Tell us about them.
questions.topic: who you are most like in your family

questions.text: Do you have a best friend?
followups: What do you like about them?

questions.text: Who do you spend time with after school?
questions.topic: who you spend time with after school

questions.text: Tell us about a good teacher you've had.
questions.topic: a good teacher you have had

questions.text: What's your favourite subject at school?

followups: What do you like to read?

questions.text: Do you enjoy using the internet in your free time?
questions.topic: using the internet in your free time

questions.text: Tell us about the things you like doing at the weekend.
questions.topic: things you like doing at the weekend

questions.text: Are there any nice places to go in your area?
questions.topic: nice places to go in your area

questions.text: Have you been anywhere nice recently?
questions.topic: somewhere nice you have been recently

questions.text: Where would you like to go for your next holiday?
followups: Why would you like to go there?
questions.topic: where you would like to go for your next holiday

2.opening: In this part of the test, I'm going to give each of you two photographs. I'd like you to talk about your photographs on your own for about a minute, and also to answer a question about your partner's photographs.

task1.title: Trying to win
photo_descriptions: a professional tennis player serving in a packed stadium in front of a huge crowd
young girls sprinting closely together on a running track during a race
task1.intro: {candidate}, it's your turn first. Here are your photographs. They show people trying to win in different situations.
task1.prompt: I'd like you to compare the photographs, and say what you think might be difficult for the people about trying to win in these situations.
task1.card_question: What might be difficult for the people about trying to win in these situations?
task1.compare_followup: Which of these sports do you think puts more pressure on the competitor, and why?
task1.followup_to_partner: {partner}, which sport would you prefer to do? Why?
task1.topic: trying to win in different sports

task2.title: Spending time outside
photo_descriptions: a large group of teenagers having a picnic around tables in a sunny park
a few teenage friends strolling down a town street lined with cafes and shops
task2.intro: Now, {partner}, here are your photographs. They show people spending time outside in different situations.
task2.prompt: I'd like you to compare the photographs, and say what you think the people are enjoying about spending time outside in these situations.
task2.card_question: What are the people enjoying about spending time outside in these situations?
task2.partner_monologue: Both photographs show young people enjoying each other's company outdoors, although the settings are quite different. In the first picture, a big group of teenagers is having a picnic in a park, sharing food and drinks under the trees, so they probably enjoy the relaxed atmosphere and being together. By contrast, the second photograph shows smaller groups of friends walking through a quiet town street past cafes. They seem to be enjoying chatting and looking around the shops at their own pace.
task2.followup_to_user: {candidate}, which of these things would you prefer to do? Why?
task2.topic: whether you would prefer a picnic in a park or walking in town

3.title: After-school classes
3.card_question: Why might students want to learn to do these skills?
3.opening: Now, I'd like you to talk about something together for about two minutes. I'd like you to imagine that a school is going to start some after-school classes to encourage their students to learn new skills. Here are some ideas for the classes and a question for you to discuss. First you have some time to look at the task.
3.start_discussion: Now, talk to each other about why students might want to learn to do these skills.
3.decision_prompt: Thank you. Now you have about a minute to decide which two would be the easiest to learn to do well.
3.topic: after-school classes to learn new skills

4.topic: after-school activities and trying new things

questions.text: Do you think classes like these would be popular with students?
questions.topic: whether after-school classes would be popular

questions.text: How important do you think it is for people to try new activities?
questions.topic: the importance of trying new activities

questions.text: Why do you think some people don't like to try new things?
questions.topic: why some people avoid trying new things

questions.text: A lot of people enjoy doing sport after school. Do you think this is a good thing?
What do students enjoy doing after school in your country?
questions.topic: what students do after school in your country

questions.text: Do you think it's better to go out and do things after school or is it better to stay at home?
questions.topic: going out versus staying at home after school

4.closing: Thank you. That is the end of the test.
